- If sentiment is consistently neutral (0.00) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% for next period.
- When sentiment is positive (e.g., 0.20), model often overshoots after a spike; cap forecast at 1–2% below true peak or adjust downward by 0.3–0.7% per day post-spike.
- Model frequently overpredicts early in 30-day horizon when price is rising; apply a 0.5–1.0% downward bias for first 5–7 days of forecast.
- If true price rises sharply after a low, model often fails to capture the momentum; add 0.2–0.5% lagged momentum adjustment to forecast.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon; if forecast is >1.5% above recent 7-day average, reduce by 0.3–0.8% per day until convergence.
- Sentiment = 0.00 implies no market bias; model should not assume upward trend; use 7-day moving average as baseline for correction.
